classification.difficultyReason: Part a needs the student to solve sin(x-π/6)=0 and to shift the interval to -π/6≤x-π/6≤11π/6 so that only two roots are kept, a small but real decision. Part b is signposted by 'Hence' and uses the intercepts as limits. It then asks for a routine integral of a shifted sine with a linear argument and exact evaluation, and the region lies above the axis, so no sign or symmetry handling is needed. There is no sketch and no inequality reasoning. This is a linked routine procedure at about the level of p36-q12 (cosine intercepts then exact area), a little above p27-q5-block, and below p47-q32, which requires inequality reasoning that makes integral comparisons.
